title: Scoped negative result: coupled partial read exchanges on P6k4
body:
PR #699's read-exchange notes leave simultaneous partial exchanges across different entering-copy pairs unexplored. This **scoped negative result / research note** checks a precisely defined part of that space: all two-pair partial choices on its pinned P6k4 input, plus a bounded three-pair follow-up. **No κ improvement is claimed.**

All **175,456 two-pair group/mask cases** and **27,344 cases across 16 connected triples in the direct-target overlap graph** violate a target hyperplane under the inherited frame-floor policy. These are parameterized cases, potentially including duplicate completed rewrites. The triple graph is a search restriction, not a proof of circuit independence.

The primary reduced-basis implementation and a separate explicit-vector-set implementation independently reconstruct eligibility and enumerate every case. Their ordered, per-candidate first-refusal digests agree exactly; the second also records explicit nonorthogonal-vector witnesses. Both reconstruct the known full SW4 word byte for byte. The independent checker verifies its exact rational B map on all 728 input columns and the complete frame profile and helper boundaries.

### Reproduce offline

Python 3.11+, standard library only:

```sh
python3 -B -I research/complex-read-exchange/verify.py
```

Expected final line:

```text
PASS: 202800 coupled partial choices rejected by both engines; exact 728-column SW4 control; no new kappa
```

The scoped package includes the pinned reconstructed input, unchanged inherited SW4 recipe/notices, deterministic evidence, both implementations, 13 mathematical failure tests, source/overlap records, and reconstruction/validation receipts.

### Validation and limits

- Fresh #699/#635 construction through P6k4 and SW4 passed content pins, native transport, ledgers, local replay, wrappers, inherited mutation controls, and the independent forward/dual 728-column audit.
- Both complete new domains and independent refusal replays passed on Python 3.11.13. The complete public command, including all 13 tests, also passed in isolated optimized Python 3.13.4.
- Scalar corruption, frame corruption, missing compensation, altered helper boundaries, conflicting edits, non-dyadic coefficients, and unfinished/truncated evidence fail closed.
- The selected-record/source-inventory check passes. No supplier, selected certificate, root Makefile or `upstream/` file changes. Full repository, phase, bit-supplier and global owner/assembly replays were not repeated for this standalone negative result. Remote CI remains separate.

The exclusion fixes the input, eligible-copy/insertion rules, untouched full SW4 moves, helper identities/boundaries, and frame-floor policy. It does not cover arbitrary triples or larger groups, alternative insertion positions, all-full combinations, relaxed floors, moved boundaries, or different decoders. No candidate passed frames, so no new κ admission was attempted. This is not a proof-assistant formalization or full multiplication-theorem audit.

Base: `66849e1475c930fd7732b1a0067ffee7e1e95f60`; #699 source: `03e8d7ca494a083e5053cd6b1228f66b98414479`; #635 dependency: `a6895a69f8ad98ab45777b03e9e6f48888c39f6f`. The final overlap refresh covered 586 open PRs through #767. Concurrent #741 improves full SW4 through eight frame coalescences and is distinct. #699's later `f042731c` change touches README/MANIFEST only; the construction inputs are unchanged.

Credit to Jeremy Kothe and the BRoute read-exchange construction, Chafik Boukhalfa's owner map and concurrent #741, icekylinx's factory, #589's bit supplier and the retained upstream lineage. Prepared for Jason Willems (@at1as) with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance and separate AI reviews. Apache-2.0; no independent human-review or priority claim. Deliberately selected complex track, OS diversification seed 21; local claim because no pinned sprint issue exists. This is separate from completed PR #666.
